label: Figure 19.7: Crowding out — extreme view
alt: Loanable funds market with a vertical supply curve SLF. Demand shifts right from D1 to D2, raising the interest rate from i1 to i2 with no rise in total lending QLF1; private borrowing falls to QLF2.
caption: With a fixed (vertical) supply of loanable funds S<sub>LF</sub>, the rightward shift of demand from D<sub>1</sub> to D<sub>2</sub> only raises the interest rate from i<sub>1</sub> to i<sub>2</sub>. Total lending stays at Q<sub>LF1</sub>, so the extra government borrowing displaces private borrowing, which falls to Q<sub>LF2</sub>: crowding out is complete.
